source.label: FY2024 Form 10-K, Item 2, Properties
source.quote: We also operate two private destinations which we utilize as ports-of-call on certain itineraries: (i) an island we own in the Bahamas that we call CocoCay; and (ii) Labadee, a secluded peninsula that we lease on the north coast of Haiti.

notes: Workforce from the FY2024 10-K (Dec 31, 2024): ~106,000 employees, of which 4,250 shoreside staff are U.S.-based and everyone else (4,850 shoreside, 95,150 shipboard, 1,750 at private destinations) is international, recorded as one region. Country shares are of the shoreside workforce (U.S. 47%, Philippines 34%, Mexico 6%, U.K. 4%). The 10-K also says the shipboard crew comes mostly from the Philippines (33%), Indonesia (17%) and India (15%); that is crew nationality, not where people work, so it is kept out of the rows. The 10-K describes two operating private destinations (CocoCay, owned; Labadee, leased); planned ones not open in FY2024 (Royal Beach Club Paradise Island, Nassau, expected 2025; Royal Beach Club Cozumel, 2026; Perfect Day Mexico, 2027; a Silversea hotel in Puerto Williams, Chile) and terminal interests (20% of the PortMiami terminal entity; iCON partnership terminals in Italy and Spain) are left out of sites. No state data.
